introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP TWO - TASK I (20 marks)**

The following is an article written by an NGO to encourage child education. It is printed in the paper as the model of the finished document.

> **IMPORTANCE OF EDUCATION IN OUR LIFE**
>
> Education is a constitutional right of every citizen that prepares an individual to play their role as a sophisticated member of society. The importance of education can be implied by habituating the lack of its existence.
>
> The importance of education and its significance can be understood through the life of an ignorant and illiterate person, who has never had the chance to visit the school and is experiencing the bane of illiteracy could value the answer to the question '***Why is Education an essential factor in our life?***' He/she knows the prominence and importance of education and its changes in an individual's life.
>
> The enormous hardship of illiteracy is its constant dependency issue. An illiterate individual depends on others for his/her survival. Education prepares its wings to fly and explore the surroundings while being confident and opportunistic. Education builds individuals, educated individuals build better societies, and better societies build great nations.
>
> *[Banner in decorative lettering, between two horizontal rules: CHILD'S RIGHTS FOUNDATION]*

Page de garde vérifiée : GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, ORDINARY LEVEL EXAMINATION, COMPUTER SCIENCE, 0595, Paper number 3, juin 2025, deux heures et demie. Chaque version a trois tâches : Task I (traitement de texte, 20 points), Task II (tableur, 20 points) et Task III (programme C ou Pascal, 10 points). Transcrites en douze fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1 à G4-T3 ; groupes ["GROUP 1"] à ["GROUP 4"] ; regles_choix vide : le sujet dit « Do all the tasks » ; le candidat ne passe qu'un seul groupe (non exprimable) et, à la Task III, choisit le programme C ou le programme Pascal (non exprimable non plus).
Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tête (numéro de centre, nom du candidat, cadre « For examiners' use only »), les lignes à compléter et les artefacts du scanner sont ignorés.

Aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur) n'a été exécuté : les menus et les étapes sont donnés de mémoire, sous une forme générale, sans citer de version de logiciel, et ne sont pas testés. Les formules de tableur ont été traduites en Python et calculées sur les données du sujet ; les résultats annoncés dans les corrigés en sont recopiés.
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : les réponses sont rédigées. Les « marking ideas » sont des répartitions indicatives faites d'après les points imprimés ; le barème du jury n'est pas connu.
Les fichiers de travail du jour (documents, classeurs, images) ne figurent pas dans le PDF : les corrigés donnent la démarche exacte et n'inventent aucune valeur de ces fichiers.

Task I : l'article (page 8 du PDF) est le modèle du document fini ; il est recopié tel qu'imprimé, la question entre guillemets simples étant en gras italique. Le bandeau « CHILD'S RIGHTS FOUNDATION » en lettres décoratives est l'image « edupower » fournie le jour de l'examen : elle n'est pas reproduite (non indispensable à la résolution) et seulement décrite entre crochets. Question 5 : « the top and bottom horizontal rules as shown » est lu comme un trait sous le titre (règle du haut) et un trait en bas de document sous l'image (règle du bas), d'après le modèle imprimé ; le sujet ne les décrit pas autrement.

Points imprimés : 2 + 5 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 20, comme l'en-tête. Les étapes 1, 6 et 7 (lancer, enregistrer, imprimer) n'ont pas de points. Le sujet regroupe les puces de la question 4 ; la numérotation 4a à 4e est ajoutée pour la transcription.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch the word processing software that is installed on your computer.
questions.corrige_markdown: Click the *Start* menu (or the icon on the desktop) and open the word processor installed on the computer; a new blank document appears. No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Set the left, right, top and bottom page margins to 2.0 cm each.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*Layout* (or *Page Layout*) > *Margins* > **Custom Margins**. In the *Page Setup* box type **2 cm** in the four boxes *Top*, *Bottom*, *Left* and *Right*, then click *OK*.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* margins box opened (1); the four margins at 2.0 cm (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Type the text of the article given above. Save as Task I  *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Type the **title** **IMPORTANCE OF EDUCATION IN OUR LIFE** and the **three paragraphs** exactly as printed, then save with *File* > *Save As* > **Task I**.

- Do **not** press *Enter* at the end of each line: the text wraps by itself; press *Enter* only at the end of the title and at the end of each paragraph.
- Respect the capital letters, the punctuation, the quotation marks around the question *Why is Education an essential factor in our life?* and the form **He/she**, **his/her**.
- Read the typed text against the paper (spelling mistakes are penalised) and use the automatic spelling check to catch typing errors.

The banner **CHILD'S RIGHTS FOUNDATION** is the picture *edupower* that is inserted in question 4.

*Marking idea (5 marks):* title (1); paragraph 1 (1); paragraph 2 (1); paragraph 3 (1); text saved as Task I (1) - indicative split, one mark lost for every few typing errors.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Format the text of the article as directed below:

- Title: Bold, Font Size of 18, Center between the left and right page margins  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select the title and apply: **Bold** (Ctrl+B), *Font Size* **18**, and **Center** (Ctrl+E), which centres the title between the left and right margins.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* bold and size 18 (1); centred (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Body: Set line spacing to 1.5, the spacing before paragraphs to 0, and the spacing after paragraphs to 12 points.  *[3 marks]*
- Apply full justification to the paragraphs as shown.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
With the three paragraphs selected click **Justify** (or press Ctrl+J): both the left and the right edges of the text are straight, as in the model.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the paragraphs selected (1); justify applied (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Use Drop Caps by 2 lines for the first letter of the first two paragraphs.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click in the first paragraph, then *Insert* > **Drop Cap** > *Drop Cap Options*; choose **Dropped** and set **Lines to drop: 2**. Do the same in the second paragraph. The third paragraph is left without a drop cap.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* drop cap on the first paragraph over 2 lines (1); same on the second paragraph (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: - Insert the image *edupower.* (provided in the candidate folder) centered at the bottom of the document as shown.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click at the end of the last paragraph and press *Enter* to get a new line. *Insert* > **Pictures** > *This Device*, browse to the candidate folder and choose **edupower**. Select the new line (or the picture) and click **Center** so that the picture is centred between the margins at the bottom of the text.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* picture inserted from the candidate folder (1); centred at the bottom (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Add the top and bottom horizontal rules as shown.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the model a horizontal line closes the title (the top rule) and a second horizontal line closes the document under the picture (the bottom rule). Click in the title and use *Home* > **Borders** > **Bottom Border**; click in the paragraph that holds the picture and apply *Borders* > **Bottom Border** again (or *Insert* > *Shapes* > *Line*, or *Borders* > *Horizontal Line* at the two places).

*Marking idea (2 marks):* top rule (1); bottom rule (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Save your work as Task I.
questions.corrige_markdown: Use *File* > **Save As** (or *Save*) and give the file the name **Task I**, in the working (candidate) folder. No mark is printed for this step, but a file that is not saved cannot be marked.

Use *File* > **Print** (or Ctrl+P), check the preview (all the formatting must be visible on the printed page), choose the printer and click *Print*. The printed sheet is inserted in the answer booklet. No mark is printed for this step.
